must_fix: CLARITY (must fix): l24 (b11, Mausi), '[calm] This one doesn't scare, beta.' Using 'scare' without an object and without 'easily' is an American idiom, not Mausi's plain small-town Indian English. In Indian English 'scare' usually takes an object, so the line comes across as 'he doesn't scare anyone'. Coming right after Kiran's 'You knew, Mausi?' and a warm 'beta', it is easily heard as comfort ('he's not scary'), which is the opposite of the Hindi 'ये डरने वाला नहीं है'. It is the first step in Mausi's reasoning: he can't be scared off and robbed the usual way, so he has to die. Fix: '[calm] This one won't get scared, beta.' Keep the tag. Raise target_seconds from 3.0 to 3.2 (32 characters at Mausi's slow pace). target_total_seconds goes from 129.5 to 129.7. In writer_notes, spoken becomes 100.6 s and dialogue about 1,102 characters. No other line changes.
